TimeIndex operators¶

Back to TimeIndex API Reference

Signature¶

std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& stream, const TimeIndex& index)

Stream Insertion¶

TimeIndex deliberately has one domain-specific operator: stream insertion. Arithmetic between temporal values belongs to Timeline and Duration; index search, union, and alignment are named operations whose policies cannot be expressed clearly by punctuation.

operator<< writes the same default structural representation as pluss::timeindex::print(index). It includes the one-dimensional shape, timezone, and readable timestamp values, returns the original stream, and does not mutate or transfer ownership from the index.

The default representation prints whole seconds. It is diagnostic text, not a round-trip serialization and not proof of nanosecond equality. Use host() for exact epoch nanoseconds or the underlying Timeline’s formatting facilities for controlled fractional output.

Examples¶

Example 1. Write an index directly.

auto index = pluss::timeindex::make({
    "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-03T00:00:00Z", "2025-01-04T00:00:00Z",
    "2025-01-05T00:00:00Z"});
std::cout << index << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[5], tz=UTC)
[ 2025-01-01 00:00:00, 2025-01-02 00:00:00, 2025-01-03 00:00:00, 2025-01-04 00:00:00, 2025-01-05 00:00:00 ]

Example 2. Stream chaining works because the operator returns the same stream.

std::ostringstream out;
auto& returned = (out << index);
returned << "\ncount=" << index.size();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << (&returned == &out) << "\n";

Output¶

true

Example 3. Choose print() when layout options are needed; stream insertion always uses defaults.

pluss::TimelinePrintOptions options;
options.format = "%F";
options.max_cols = 3;
options.edge_items = 1;
options.show_tz = false;
std::cout << pluss::timeindex::print(index, options) << "\n";

Output¶

TimeIndex(shape=[5])
[ 2025-01-01, ..., 2025-01-05 ]

Cost¶

Rendering formats every lane before applying display truncation, so cost is linear in size() even when an ellipsis is shown. Stream insertion avoids the returned std::string object used by the string-returning print overload but still creates formatted lane text internally.
